answer: I would anchor trust in Proof of unique jury duty summons history. With summons answered in one county over years, a single wander check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so summons answered in one county over years stays private; the ledge is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the sable of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
